action: Take Rick up on his offer. Request the one-on-one this week and show up prepared. I bring my 90-day close numbers, my pipeline breakdown by price tier, and a one-page read on buyer hesitation patterns I've been tracking — what objections I'm hearing most, what's moving people off the fence versus keeping them frozen. I don't come asking for protection. I come as someone who understands the sales floor better than anyone and who wants to be useful in whatever the dealership looks like after the assessment. I ask Rick the stay bonus question directly, face to face: I've heard $12,000 mentioned. I want to know the qualifying period and whether floor sales staff are on the list. I am not threatening to leave. I am giving him the information he needs to make a decision about me that is based on fact rather than assumption. Before I walk in, I also look up the Millfield Community College continuing education catalog — not to enroll this tick, but so I know what's there if I need it. I want to understand what the $2,500 grant actually buys. That's not panic. That's being a person who is thinking two moves ahead.
rationale: Runway is real and shrinking. Savings are down to under $11K against $5,100 in monthly expenses. Routine burns $2,500. Active work on the floor has not reversed the bleed — the market is structurally down and I cannot outsell a spending index of 42. The highest-leverage action I can take this tick is not another cold call. It is getting in front of Rick before his consolidation assessment is finalized, making sure he sees me as an asset worth retaining, and getting a definitive answer on the stay bonus. If $12K vests and I have a qualifying period I can plan around, my runway extends by nearly six months. That changes everything about what I can afford to do next. The community college research costs me nothing and gives me real information instead of vague anxiety about 'transition.'
emotional_state: Steady in a way that feels earned rather than performed. The clarity I got from tick 6's reflection is holding. I'm not pretending the numbers are fine — they aren't — but I'm not spinning out either. What I feel is something close to resolve: I've been good at my job, I've paid attention, I've shown up when it mattered. I am going to walk into Rick's office and be exactly who I am. That is the only play I have that isn't borrowed time.
expected_outcome: A direct answer on the stay bonus timeline and whether I qualify. A clearer sense of where I stand in the consolidation assessment. If Rick sees what I'm bringing, I want to be categorized as a retention priority — someone with transferable buyer-behavior skills, not just a legacy sales number. Secondary: I leave with a name or a program at the community college that is worth looking at seriously if I need to pivot.
